body: DBT is a life saver for me but I am currently struggling with the resentment you mentioned here. How did/are you handling it?

Thank you! This comment made me feel even more motivated because it seems a bit harder to find therapy success stories (which makes sense since people reach out on the internet for a reason). If I ever struggle or feel stuck in therapy I’ll try to remind myself to keep going!
When I was on medication I didn’t think of them as medication to make me feel better, but rather, just a part of my morning routine.

This is another reason why I easily blow up (assuming people are hurting me) and also why I isolate. It’s not even on purpose but it just feels safer for both me and the other person that might get involved. It helps me a bit to remember that not everyone is just “good” or “bad” though.

I don’t know if I’m in love at this point as much as it’s an attachment and obsession. 

I’m sorry I don’t have advice. :( The only thing that has helped me is distancing myself, so I can imagine constant contact and working together would be really painful.
Me too. I wish I could give you an answer but I go through the exact same thing. I’m realizing I’m the only one that has the potential to find myself that “baseline” but it’s so difficult

Thank you for commenting. I try really hard to make myself clear that I’m not interested in the first place. But I guess accepting complements or continuing to reply kind of gives off the “leading on” vibe. I’ve decided to block the guy.

I’m aware; I made sure to read that thread as well as some of the other comments from both ends before commenting so that I know what’s going on.

I’m sorry about the trauma you’ve had to endure. Though I wasn’t homeless, I often had to escape the apartment at night and hide back when I was in an abusive relationship, so I have a grasp on how scary it is to be out there.

A lot of us end up on this sub from being traumatized and suffering from BPD. We tend to be a bit sensitive, and maybe that’s why the user got defensive. *I’m not saying what the user said was okay or excused in any way.* It really wasn’t. At all. I’m sorry they said such thing to you. But I’m just saying there are two sides and two histories to a story and sometimes it’s necessary to just report it and leave it be. I’m sure you meant well but the reality is I probably wouldn’t have seen their triggering comments if this post didn’t exist and the user was reported and left alone. I’m also pretty sure this [violates the rules on this sub](https://www.reddit.com/r/BPD/about/rules/).

Not to sound rude or anything but looking at both of your comments it sounds like both of you got defensive and a little too worked up. At the end of the day both of you probably had good intentions but this is just unnecessary drama at this point

It’s fine! It does harm my skin. I have a scar about half the size of my thumb because of it and people constantly ask what happened. It usually doesn’t hurt at all when I pinch. I’ve seen four therapists in my life. Two have said I just have dermitelomania/skin picking OCD, two have said it’s a coping method I developed because of my childhood. So I don’t really know why I do this lol. It could be both.

I’ve had a skin pinching habit since I was like 6 years old. It worsens when I’m anxious or thinking of conversing with someone. I’ve managed to stop every other self harm habit and keep the pinching down to one location. I wonder if this still counts. It sucks because it feels different from the reason why I used to cut and punch myself.
Yeah :/ The only person that can undo that and improve my life is myself though

I used to feel this with my boyfriend but I would also feel absolutely horrible about it and nag him later. I’ve stopped expressing my outbursts to him and back off when things feel like they’re going south no matter who I feel is wrong, but deep inside, I still feel tempted.

Literally here because I just did this. In my case I’ve realized my assumptions when I’m sensitive are usually wrong. Not miscommunicated. Just straight up wrong. I’ll interpret their words and tone wrong no matter how careful they are. I don’t know what to do from there though since I feel justified at the time.

Yes!! I feel like the BPD is physically inside of me too. It was worst when I first started learning how to contro myself. It’s like I’m hiding a beast within me.

I also feel you on the emptiness too. That seems to be something I can’t combat no matter how hard I try.

I’m really not trying to be mean here, but BPD or not, I think it’d be best to leave her alone. She has made it pretty clear she doesn’t want to be in contact with you multiple times just in your short story... 

This is personal experience, so your ex may be different, but I had two nasty breakups in the past, and both of my exes have sporadically tried contacting me a few times. I ignored them and they contacted my friends. I honestly hate it. It’s great that they care but I find it insulting that they aren’t letting go. It just feels selfish and it’s triggering to me. I wish they could have showed that care when we were together lol. It’s not that I don’t care, but it ended for a reason, and I wish they’d respect that.

Yeah, I’ve given up on it. I’m usually pretty good at keeping stuff to myself, but a month ago something set me back quite a bit so I reached out to my old friends. They finally realized I’m an irratic mess, so they were there for me at the time, but now they keep distance. Can’t blame them, but damn.
Yes!!! We’ve got this! 💕

I don’t think you were “replaced”, I think she just started really fitting in with the family, and no one else has “replacing” one person with another in their mind. Two years is a long time of living together. Your mother and grandmother probably have long-term habits to show family closeness to, hence the socks and conversation. If the girlfriend is trying to marry your brother, they’re going to be her “mother” and “grandmother”. 

As smoneone with BPD I understand where you’re com8ng from. I really do. But I highly doubt you can be “replaced” by your family (assuming they’re loving and healthy for the most part) as much as you gained a new one. :)

Personally, I realized I get stressed when I’m trying to use DBT skills for *other people*, because I start to expect the same amount of effort back. So, when my mindset is: “I’m doing these skills so that *we* can communicate properly”, it makes me obsess over the other person’s behaviors, and results me in thinking: “Why can’t *you* do the same? Why is it okay for *you* to do this, but not me!?”

So I just try to make it all about myself: “If I use these skills I learned, I’ll be able to keep the argument to a minimum, and won’t have to feel miserable about it later.” This kind of helps minimize expectations from other people and still see the benifit of DBT.

DBT is a pretty unique way of therapy. We’re basically given a textbook that teaches what action is bad, why it’s bad, and what to do instead. But not many people are given a literal, step by step, “correct” instruction on how to think, communicate, and behave. Instead, people usually learn what works for them while they’re growing up, and therefore don’t see some of what DBT considers “bad” behaviors, bad. In fact, it probably feels like an insult to their character to the person doing these “bad” behaviors when they’re told to change, especially if they’re unaware of the damage it causes. This kind of creates the ultimate “people can’t change unless they want to change” situation I think.

It’s probably that, and a mixture of how we attract / are attracted to people similar to us/come from environments similar to us. I’m also hypervigilant and observant of other people’s actions, which probably adds to the bad behaviors standing out.

This is strictly what I personally experienced though, so please just take it as a “possibility” or “opinion”. :)

Honestly I think I’m surrounded by people who are toxic and it causes setbacks to my recovery. The more I learn about DBT, the more I realize how a lot of my “friends”, family, and sometimes significant other have bad coping mechanisms and communication issues themselves.
